edges.description: Therapeutic ultraviolet phototherapy opposes the depigmented phenotype by driving repigmentation, stimulating melanocyte precursors out of the follicular reservoir to repopulate lesional skin. The target is the depigmentation phenotype rather than the melanocyte-destruction process, because repopulation after destruction is what the cited evidence measures; phototherapy's separate immunomodulatory action on the autoreactive attack is not evidenced here.

evidence.snippet: Vitiligo is an acquired cutaneous disorder of pigmentation... Recent data provide strong evidence supporting an autoimmune pathogenesis of vitiligo.

evidence.reference_title: Vitiligo in the City of Bukavu ( Democratic Republic of Congo).
evidence.snippet: Vitiligo is a skin disorder characterized by selective loss of melanocytes resulting in circumscribed, depigmented macules and patches... its effects can be psychological, leading to stigmatization and suicidal ideation.

evidence.reference_title: The definition and assessment of vitiligo: a consensus report of the Vitiligo European Task Force.
evidence.snippet: Vitiligo is the most common depigmenting disorder, which affects 0.5-1% of the worldwide population, causing disfigurement and serious disturbances in well being.

evidence.reference_title: Cumulative life course impairment in vitiligo.
evidence.snippet: Vitiligo is an acquired, idiopathic skin disease characterized by the mostly progressive loss of the inherited skin color leading to white patches... The disease burden includes stigmatization, depression, impaired quality of life, lack of self-confidence, embarrassment and self-consciousness.

nodes.description: Vitiligo produces acquired, progressive cutaneous depigmentation from loss of functional melanocytes.

evidence.snippet: common acquired depigmenting skin disease characterized by a progressive loss of functional melanocytes

nodes.description: Promotes the repigmentation process in some cases, but can exacerbate the contrast in others.

evidence.reference_title: Impact of Ultraviolet Light on Vitiligo.
evidence.snippet: This chapter focuses on the use of ultraviolet light in vitiligo as an established therapeutic option.

evidence.reference_title: Is targeted UVB as effective as excimer light phototherapy in treatment of vitiligo?
evidence.snippet: Targeted phototherapy with EL demonstrated better repigmenting efficacy than TUVB in vitiligo.

evidence.reference_title: Assessment of changes in color and size of vitiligo lesions during treatment with narrow band ultraviolet B.
evidence.snippet: Patients received Nb-UVB three times per week for 6 months... 90% of lesions showed variable degrees of repigmentation and 10% showed increase in size, indicating increased activity of the disease.
